channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran and Afghanistan advance transport diplomacy, impacting Central Asia
item.description: Iran is enhancing its transport diplomacy with Afghanistan, while also building partnerships with Central Asian states. Recent developments show Afghanistan's active role in Eurasian overland routes, supported by China's Belt and Road Initiative. Uzbekistan is expected to benefit from diversified logistics and southern transit corridors.

item.title: Journalist Mahabat Tajibek kyzy's trial postponed again due to expert absence
item.description: The trial of journalist Mahabat Tajibek kyzy in Bishkek was postponed again to October 6 because experts from the Ministry of Justice's forensic service did not appear. One expert is on sick leave, another is on a business trip, and a third has resigned. The defense requested an independent specialist be questioned if experts remain absent.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Aurubis discuss copper scrap processing projects
item.description: Kazakhstan and Aurubis AG have discussed cooperation in processing copper scrap and technogenic mineral formations within the country. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Aurubis supervisory board chairman Fritz Wahrenholt reviewed prospects for joint investment projects in Kazakhstan's mining and metallurgical complex. Both sides prioritized complex processing of copper-containing raw materials and secondary processing development.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Belarus to Enhance Inter-Parliamentary Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Belarus held their third Inter-Parliamentary Commission meeting in Khiva, focusing on strengthening strategic partnership through dialogue. Discussions included expanding trade, economic, and investment ties, and implementing agreements reached at the highest level.

item.title: Money Transfers from Kazakhstan Abroad Halved in August
item.description: In August, 27.9 billion tenge were sent abroad from Kazakhstan via international money transfer systems (IMTS), half the amount sent in July. The National Bank's data, cited by DATA HUB, indicates this was the lowest figure since January 2016, adjusted for inflation. Russia and Uzbekistan saw significant drops in transfers.

item.title: Uzbek President Awards State Prizes to Teachers, Announces Education Reforms
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with educators ahead of Teacher and Mentor Day, presenting state awards. He proposed establishing the Abdulla Avloniy state award for advanced teachers and emphasized education's crucial role in building a New Uzbekistan. The president noted significant infrastructure development and the importance of content quality.

item.title: Youth Parliaments of Uzbekistan and Belarus Sign Roadmap for Cooperation
item.description: The Youth Parliament of Uzbekistan and the Youth Council of Belarus signed a roadmap during a joint meeting within the Uzbek-Belarusian inter-parliamentary forum. Discussions focused on expanding youth participation in governance, inclusive education, and cooperation between youth parliaments, including digital technologies and employment support.

item.title: KazMunayGas Aims to Extract Additional 155 Million Tons of Oil from Existing Fields
item.description: KazMunayGas plans to extract up to an additional 155 million tons of oil from 12 priority fields by the end of their lifecycle. The company is implementing a strategy to increase oil recovery, including the use of digital twins, and is also pursuing extensive geological exploration with international partners.

item.title: Taliban Minister States No Obstacles for Afghans Wishing to Return Home
item.description: Noorullah Noori, the Taliban's minister of borders and tribal affairs, announced that Afghans who left the country can return without facing obstacles. He cautioned returnees against disrupting the country. This statement contrasts with reports from Hasht-e Subh Daily citing detentions and killings of former military personnel after their forced return.

item.title: Israel's Defense Minister Claims FlyDubai Flight Incident Was Terror Attempt
item.description: Israel's Defense Minister stated that a FlyDubai flight incident was an attempted terror act. The attacker reportedly intended to crash the plane with all passengers. Other pilots aboard helped land the aircraft. The second pilot was detained in Saudi Arabia. The incident is under investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Improves Position in Global Innovation Index
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has moved up to 92nd place in the 2026 Global Innovation Index, from 96th previously. The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) attributes this progress to improvements in innovation outputs, particularly in knowledge, technology, and creative outcomes. Strengths include human capital, education spending, student mobility, and creative sectors.

item.title: Car import regulations streamlined, no price increase expected
item.description: An expert meeting discussed car import and registration procedures. Officials clarified rules for individuals and businesses, emphasizing that basic import requirements remain unchanged. The changes aim to streamline processes and align regulations.

item.title: Kazakh President meets with Bavarian Prime Minister Markus Söder
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Bavarian Prime Minister Markus Söder, expressing appreciation for Bavaria's economic strength and innovation. Tokayev highlighted opportunities for integrating Bavaria's technological achievements with Kazakhstan's resources and industrial potential.

item.title: Tokayev praises Putin in Germany; Kyrgyzstan aids Russia sanctions evasion, says NYT
item.description: President Tokayev praised Putin during a visit to Germany. The New York Times reported that Kyrgyzstan is helping Russia evade sanctions. Separately, a plane flying from Dubai to Israel declared an emergency and landed in Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Kazakhstan's People's Council: Appointed Members, Potential Influence
item.description: Kazakhstan's newly formed People's Council has begun its work. Its members were appointed by the president, not elected by the public. The council can propose draft laws to parliament and initiate referendums. President Tokayev stated the body aims to convey diverse public opinions to the authorities.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Meets with Bavarian Prime Minister Markus Söder
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Bavarian Prime Minister Markus Söder. Tokayev highlighted Bavaria's economic power and innovation potential, viewing it as a key partner for Kazakhstan's economic modernization and diversification. Both leaders emphasized strengthening transport links to foster closer economic ties between Kazakhstan and Germany.

item.title: UN Secretary-General Urges Global Cooperation to Eliminate Nuclear Weapons
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for international cooperation to reduce nuclear risks and achieve the goal of eliminating nuclear weapons. He noted the absence of limits on strategic nuclear arsenals, which weakens global security. Guterres urged all nations to actively participate in disarmament efforts.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Export Agency Supports Shymkent's Manufacturing Sector Expansion
item.description: Kazakh enterprises in the manufacturing industry are expanding into foreign markets. The Export-Credit Agency of Kazakhstan (ECA) is assisting businesses, like the Shymkent industrial hub, by addressing challenges such as working capital shortages and non-payment risks from foreign clients. ECA's support has reached 28.5 billion tenge for 'Shymkentmay'.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Sees Great Potential for Partnership with Bavaria
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated there is significant potential for combining Bavaria's technological capabilities with Kazakhstan's resources and industrial capacity. He views Bavaria as a key partner for modernizing and diversifying Kazakhstan's economy. Strengthening transport links was also highlighted as important for closer economic ties.

item.title: Israel calls Fly Dubai plane incident a 'terrorist attempt'
item.description: Israel's Defense Minister described an incident on a Fly Dubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv as a jihadist terrorist attempt. He stated that Israeli passengers prevented the attacker from crashing the plane. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reported that Saudi authorities are investigating the pilot.

item.title: Six banks in Kazakhstan lower deposit interest rates in September
item.description: Six banks in Kazakhstan reduced their deposit interest rates in September, influenced by a decrease in the base rate to 16.25%. One bank raised its rate for demand deposits to 16.08%, the highest in the segment. The average market rate remained unchanged at 14.99%.

item.title: Almaty introduces paid parking for illegally parked vehicles from October 4
item.description: Almaty will implement paid parking fees for vehicles impounded for administrative offenses and stored in municipal lots starting October 4. The evacuation cost is set at 3 MCI (12,975 tenge) for all vehicle categories. Light vehicle storage costs 2.5 MCI for the first day and 5 MCI for subsequent days.

item.title: Tashkent begins renovation program, handing over new apartments to residents
item.description: Tashkent has launched its renovation program, with the first phase commencing on September 29. Keys to new apartments were handed over to participants of the renovation program in the "Yangi Oʻzbekiston" residential complex in Sergeli district.

item.title: US Supreme Court Allows Trump Administration to Resume Deporting Migrants to Third Countries
item.description: The US Supreme Court has permitted the Trump administration to resume deporting migrants to third countries without allowing them to appeal based on human rights grounds. The court has not yet made a final decision on the legality of this procedure, with full hearings scheduled for December and a ruling expected by July 2027. Approximately 25,000 migrants have been deported under this program.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Discusses Potential $500 Million Investment Projects with Linde
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Linde GmbH's Senior Vice President Oliver Pfann to discuss new projects with potential investments up to $500 million. They noted the signing of an agreement for a new air separation unit in Temirtau and explored joint ventures in the petrochemical industry. Tokayev also highlighted Kazakhstan's interest in Linde's carbon capture and hydrogen infrastructure developments.

item.title: Russia Restricts Cash Ruble Exports to Tajikistan and Other Countries
item.description: Russia has limited the export of cash rubles to several countries, including Tajikistan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan, and Uzbekistan. Individuals can no longer export more than 1 million rubles in cash, while businesses face stricter limits. The decree, signed by President Putin, took effect on September 29.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Belarus Discuss Inter-Parliamentary Dialogue and Economic Cooperation
item.description: The Speaker of the Senate of Uzbekistan, Tanzila Narbaeva, met with the Chairperson of the Council of the Republic of Belarus, Natalya Kochanova, to discuss inter-parliamentary cooperation. They emphasized strengthening ties, identifying new areas of interaction, and boosting trade-economic relations, including in agriculture and manufacturing. Cooperation in organized labor migration was also addressed.

item.title: Taxi Driver Deported from Kazakhstan After Passenger Complaint
item.description: A taxi driver in Petropavlovsk has been deported from Kazakhstan following a passenger's complaint about rudeness. The 42-year-old Tajik citizen was found to be violating migration laws and was sentenced to one day of administrative arrest and subsequent expulsion. This marks his second violation within a year, leading to a five-year entry ban.

item.title: New Limits Introduced on Annual Interest Rates for Auto Leasing in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan has set maximum annual effective interest rates for auto leasing contracts with individuals. The Ministry of Industry approved new rates: 36% for vehicles up to 20 million tenge, and 46% for vehicles exceeding 20 million tenge. If the lessor is a bank, the rate must not exceed 35% annually. These regulations take effect October 9, 2026.

item.title: Tajikistan Begins Autumn Military Conscription Period for Conscripts
item.description: Tajikistan's autumn military conscription period starts October 1 and runs until November 30. Young men born between 1999 and 2008, who are eligible for service, will be drafted into the armed forces. This conscription drive occurs twice annually, in spring and autumn, for individuals aged 18 to 27.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Tax Exemption for Private School Tuition Fees
item.description: Parents in Uzbekistan paying for private school education will see their tax-exempt income doubled from 3 million to 6 million soums. President Mirziyoyev announced this measure, which aims to save families between 6-7 million soums annually. A system for automatic monthly refunds to tax authorities will be implemented.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Calls Putin a 'Suitable Politician for the World'
item.description: During his visit to Germany, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev described Russian leader Vladimir Putin as a 'suitable politician for the whole world.' Tokayev also expressed great respect for the Ukrainian people, their history, culture, traditions, and language, calling for a temporary cessation of hostilities.

item.title: Large-scale modernization continues at Uch-Kurgan HPP, increasing capacity
item.description: Large-scale modernization is underway at the Uch-Kurgan Hydroelectric Power Plant (HPP), aiming to update equipment and boost its installed capacity. The Ministry of Energy reported that these upgrades will enhance the station's overall performance and output.

item.title: UN-Habitat rehabilitates Afghan health facilities with JICA support
item.description: UN-Habitat is rehabilitating health facilities in impoverished areas of Afghanistan to improve healthcare access, with support from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). The initiative aims to provide better services for patients and opportunities for doctors.

item.title: Russia claims overnight strikes hit Ukraine's energy and communications facilities
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Defense announced that its forces conducted a large-scale overnight strike targeting energy and communications facilities supporting Ukraine's military industry in Kyiv. Precision-guided weapons and drones were reportedly used in the attack.

item.title: Taliban Minister Urges Armed Opponents to Return and Negotiate
item.description: Taliban Minister of Borders and Tribal Affairs Noorullah Noori called on armed opposition groups to return to Afghanistan and engage in dialogue. He questioned their political goals if the Taliban were overthrown and urged them to clarify their intentions, describing them as "slaves" but also capable of negotiation.

item.title: Siemens Expresses Readiness to Participate in Data Center Infrastructure Development in Kazakhstan
item.description: Siemens is prepared to participate in developing data center infrastructure in Kazakhstan, as stated by Vice President Bernd Ulbrich during a meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The company can offer technological solutions for modernizing power grids, digitalization, automation, and water supply, aligning with Kazakhstan's economic modernization priorities.

item.title: Uzbek President meets with FIFA President Gianni Infantino
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with FIFA President Gianni Infantino on September 30. They discussed hosting the U-20 World Cup in Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan, and cooperation on football development. FIFA's regional office in Tashkent was also discussed.

item.title: Uzbekistan President meets FIFA President, discusses hosting U-20 World Cup with Azerbaijan
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with FIFA President Gianni Infantino. The discussion focused on the possibility of co-hosting the FIFA U-20 World Cup with Azerbaijan. Further details were discussed during the meeting.

item.title: Asman Airlines explains domestic flight ticket price increase due to rising fuel costs
item.description: Asman Airlines has explained the rise in domestic flight ticket prices, citing a 95.7 percent increase in aviation fuel costs since the start of 2026, including VAT. This information was reported by 'Airports of Kyrgyzstan'.
